questions.q: You have a green light, but there is a sign 2.4 before the intersection. On your right, a green car is waiting at a red light. What should you do?
options: Give way to the green car: it is on the main road
Proceed: here the traffic lights decide the order
Stop at the sign, then proceed
Proceed only if the green car flashes its headlights
questions.explain: An intersection where the traffic lights decide the order is treated as controlled. Priority signs there apply only when the lights are off or flashing amber. You have a green light now, so proceed.

questions.q: Which of these drivers is allowed to drive past this sign?
options: A taxi driver with the taximeter switched on
A resident of a house on this street
The driver of a truck delivering goods to a shop on this street
The driver of a route bus
questions.explain: Sign 3.1 bans entry by all vehicles in that direction, except for route vehicles. The exception for residents and service vehicles applies to signs 3.2-3.8, and a taxi is not a route vehicle.

questions.q: This sign applies on a stretch of road. Does the ban also apply to vehicles entering the stretch from the opposite end?
options: No, only to those who have passed this sign
No, if they keep to their own lane while driving towards you
Only during hours of darkness
Yes: the sign bans travel in both directions
questions.explain: Signs 3.2-3.9, 3.32 and 3.33 ban travel by the relevant types of vehicle in both directions. Unlike sign 3.1, the ban does not depend on which end you entered from.
questions.ref: Annex 1, sign 3.2 and the general provisions of Chapter 3

questions.q: You are a driver with a group III disability affecting the musculoskeletal system. Are you allowed to drive past this sign?
options: Yes: this sign does not apply to such vehicles
No: the exception applies only to groups I and II
No: the exception applies only to route vehicles
Yes, but only if you live in this zone
questions.explain: Signs 3.2, 3.3 and 3.28-3.30 do not apply to vehicles driven by a person with a group I or group II disability, or a group III disability affecting the musculoskeletal system, nor to vehicles carrying such a person.

questions.q: Which of them may drive on the road beyond this sign?
options: The rider of a moped
The driver of an electric car
A cyclist
The rider of a motorcycle
questions.explain: Sign 3.3 bans travel by motor vehicles, that is self-propelled vehicles with an engine. A moped, a motorcycle and an electric car are motor vehicles, while an ordinary bicycle is powered by muscular effort.

questions.q: This sign has no plate and no figures under it. Who is it banning from driving past?
options: A bus
A truck with a maximum authorised mass of 3 t
A truck designed to carry passengers
A tractor
questions.explain: Sign 3.4 without figures bans travel by trucks and vehicle combinations with a maximum authorised mass of more than 3.5 t, and by tractors and self-propelled machines. It does not apply to buses, light trucks or trucks designed to carry passengers.

questions.q: You are driving an empty truck: its maximum authorised mass is 12 t, and its actual mass right now is 6 t. Can you drive past this sign with no figures on it?
options: Yes: right now the truck weighs only 6 t
No: the sign bans all trucks
Yes, if the truck is passing through without stopping
No: what matters is the maximum authorised mass
questions.explain: Sign 3.4 looks at the maximum authorised mass, that is the mass set by the manufacturer, not at how loaded the vehicle is. Yours is 12 t, more than 3.5 t, so driving past is banned even when empty.

questions.q: You are driving an empty truck: maximum authorised mass 12 t, actual mass right now 6 t. Can you drive past this sign?
options: No: the authorised mass is more than 10 t
No: the sign bans trucks heavier than 3.5 t
Yes: the sign limits the actual mass
Yes, if your speed is no more than 30 km/h
questions.explain: Sign 3.11 limits the total actual mass of the vehicle (together with a trailer, if any). Your empty truck weighs 6 t right now, less than 10 t, so driving past is allowed. Sign 3.4, by contrast, looks at the maximum authorised mass.

questions.q: You are riding a moped just passing through: you do not live or work in this area. Can you drive past this sign?
options: Yes: the sign applies only to motorcycles
Yes, if you ride no faster than 20 km/h
No: the sign bans both motorcycles and mopeds
Yes, if you ride in daylight with dipped headlights on
questions.explain: Sign 3.5 bans travel by motorcycles and mopeds. The exception applies only to those who live or work in the zone, or who service it: they enter at the intersection nearest to their destination.

questions.q: Can you drive past this sign on a self-propelled machine, for example a backhoe loader, if you are just passing through?
options: Yes: the sign applies only to wheeled tractors
No: both tractors and self-propelled machines are banned
Yes, if you keep to no more than 20 km/h on the shoulder
questions.explain: Sign 3.6 bans travel by tractors and self-propelled machines. The exception applies to vehicles that service businesses or residents of the zone, or that belong to its residents and workers; passing through does not fall under it.

questions.q: Which of these drivers does this sign stop from continuing?
options: The driver of a car towing a light caravan
The driver of an articulated bus
The driver of a car towing another car
The driver of a truck with no trailer
questions.explain: Sign 3.7 bans travel by trucks and tractors with a trailer of any type, and towing of motor vehicles. It does not apply to a car with a trailer, but towing a car here is not allowed.

questions.q: Can you ride a bicycle past this sign?
options: Yes: only e-scooters are banned
No: the sign bans bicycles and scooters
No: the sign bans all small vehicles
Only children under 14
questions.explain: Sign 3.9.1 bans travel only by e-scooters; it does not apply to bicycles. Bicycles, e-scooters and small electric vehicles are all banned together by a different sign, 3.9.

questions.q: Which of these is this sign not banning?
options: A cyclist
The rider of an e-scooter
The rider of a self-balancing unicycle
The rider of a moped
questions.explain: Sign 3.9 bans travel by bicycles, e-scooters and small electric vehicles, for example self-balancing unicycles and hoverboards. A moped is a motor vehicle, so this sign does not apply to it.

questions.q: The sign stands on the left side of the street, as in the diagram. Which pedestrian is breaking its requirement?
options: Only the pedestrian on the right
Only the pedestrian on the left
Both
Neither
questions.explain: Sign 3.10 bans pedestrians only on the side of the road where it is placed. The pedestrian on the right is walking on the other side of the street, so the ban does not apply to them.
questions.ref: Annex 1, sign 3.10 and the general provisions of Chapter 3

questions.q: Your truck's total mass is 11 t, split evenly as 5.5 t on each of its two axles. Can you drive past this sign?
options: No: the total mass is more than 6 t
Yes, if you keep to no more than 20 km/h
No: the sign bans trucks heavier than 6 t
Yes: the load on each axle is less than 6 t
questions.explain: Sign 3.12 limits not the total mass but the actual load on any axle. Yours is 5.5 t per axle, less than 6 t, so you may drive past.

questions.q: Your car is 4.6 m long, and together with a caravan trailer it is 11 m long. Can you drive past this sign?
options: Yes: the car itself is less than 10 m long
Yes, if the trailer is currently empty
No: the sign bans any trailer
No: the length of the whole combination counts
questions.explain: Sign 3.15 bans travel by vehicles and vehicle combinations whose overall length, laden or unladen, is more than the figure shown. Your combination is 11 m long, so driving past is banned.

questions.q: You are driving behind a truck within the zone of this sign. How must you drive?
options: No faster than 30 km/h
Keep at least 30 m from the vehicle ahead
Keep 30 m only from trucks; less is fine behind cars
questions.explain: Sign 3.16 bans travel with a following distance shorter than the figure shown on the sign. Keep at least 30 m from any vehicle ahead. The zone of application runs to the nearest intersection, unless plate 7.2.1 shortens it.
questions.ref: Annex 1, sign 3.16 and the general provisions of Chapter 3

questions.q: What must a driver do at this sign?
options: Reduce speed to 20 km/h and proceed
Proceed without stopping if no one is there
Turn on the hazard warning lights and proceed
Stop at the checkpoint
questions.explain: Sign 3.17.3 “Checkpoint” bans passing through checkpoints, for example police or transport-inspection posts, without stopping.

questions.q: There has been a crash ahead, and the road service has put up this sign. What does it require?
options: Stop: you must not go any further
Slow down and carefully drive around the danger
Proceed if the danger is not in your lane
Only trucks must stop
questions.explain: Sign 3.17.2 “Danger” bans any further travel because of a crash or other danger. You must not drive around the danger: wait until the sign is removed, or turn around where this is allowed.

questions.q: This sign stands before an intersection. Right after the intersection, on the right, there is an entrance to a yard. Can you turn in there as shown?
options: No: the sign bans any right turn
Yes: the sign applies only at this intersection
No: the ban lasts until the next intersection
No: only residents may enter the yard
questions.explain: Sign 3.18.1 applies to the crossing of carriageways before which it is placed. Once you have driven straight across the intersection, you may turn right into the yard: an exit onto an adjacent area is not an intersection.

questions.q: You have passed this sign. Ahead, a tractor is travelling at about 35 km/h, and the oncoming lane is clear. Can you overtake it?
options: Yes: a tractor is a slow-moving vehicle
Yes, if the road markings are a broken line
No: it is travelling at not less than 30 km/h
Yes, if you sound the horn
questions.explain: Sign 3.20 bans overtaking of all vehicles except single ones travelling at under 30 km/h. The tractor is doing about 35 km/h, so you may not overtake it before the end of the sign's zone.

questions.q: Driving a car, you have passed the sign, then a field track joining the road, as in the diagram. There is no central reservation. What is the highest speed you may drive?
options: 70 km/h
90 km/h
100 km/h
110 km/h
questions.explain: A place where a field or forest track joins the road does not count as an intersection, so the zone of sign 3.24 continues to the nearest real intersection. The 70 km/h limit still applies.

questions.q: Driving a car, you have passed the sign, then an intersection, as in the diagram. There is no central reservation, and there were no other signs. What is the highest speed you may drive?
options: 70 km/h
90 km/h
100 km/h
110 km/h
questions.explain: The zone of application of sign 3.24 ends at the nearest intersection beyond it. Beyond that, the general limit applies for cars outside built-up areas on a road with no central reservation: 100 km/h.

questions.q: You passed these signs 600 m back, and there have been no intersections since. Can you overtake now, if there are no other bans?
options: No: the ban lasts until the nearest intersection
No: the ban lasts until sign 3.21
Yes: the plate limited the zone to 500 metres
Yes, but only slow-moving vehicles
questions.explain: Plate 7.2.1 shortens the zone of application of sign 3.20: the overtaking ban applies only for 500 m from the sign. You have already gone 600 m, so overtaking is allowed again if there are no other bans.
